cohort: The study included 8 multiparous women (median age 36 years) who had a live birth subsequent to transvaginal sacrospinous hysteropexy due to grade 2 or higher uterine prolapse.
finding: Transvaginal sacrospinous hysteropexy is an appropriate surgical treatment method for symptomatic uterovaginal descensus in women who wish to preserve their uterus and future childbearing, with a high satisfaction rate and low recurrence.
mod_finding: All 8 pregnancies were delivered by cesarean section, which was found to be a reliable and satisfactory delivery route for these women.
gest_age: At least 37 weeks (with one preterm delivery due to twin pregnancy)
